artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{SU}_X(r)$ denote the moduli space of semistable rank-$r$ vector bundles on $X$ with trivial determinant. The Picard group of $\mathrm{SU}_X(r)$ is infinite cyclic, generated by an ample line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ called the determinant line bundle: it is characterized (up to isomorphism) by the property that for any line bundle $M$ of degree $g-1$ on $X$, the divisor 
$$\Theta_M = \{E \in \mathrm{SU}_X(r) : h^0(X, E \otimes M) \neq 0\}$$
is a divisor in the linear system $|\mathcal{L}|$.

Determine whether the linear system $|\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2}|$ associated to the second tensor power of the determinant line bundle is base-point free; that is, whether for every semistable rank-$r$ vector bundle $E$ on $X$ with trivial determinant there exists a global section $s \in H^0(\mathrm{SU}_X(r), \mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2})$ which does not vanish at the point $[E] \in \mathrm{SU}_X(r)$.
artifact.category_tag: Generalized theta functions on moduli of vector bundles
artifact.status_search_result: Effective base-point-freeness of powers $|\mathcal{L}^{k}|$ on $\mathrm{SU}_X(r)$ has been studied extensively (Le Potier, Hein, Popa, Pauly), giving explicit bounds on $k$ depending on $r$ and $g$ for which $|\mathcal{L}^k|$ is base-point free, but these bounds are far from $k=2$ in general. For $r=2$ classical results imply $|\mathcal{L}^2|$ is base-point free, and partial results exist in low rank, but a general answer for all $r$ and $g$ does not appear to be established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: On the base locus of the generalized theta divisor (Popa)
status_evidence.snippet: For r=2, or r=3 and X of genus 2 or generic of any genus, |Θ| is base point free; Raynaud constructs base points for |Θ| when r=ng with n≥2 dividing g.
status_evidence.claim: Even |L| has base points in higher rank in general; the question of |L^2| is more delicate.

status_evidence.title: Dimension estimates for Hilbert schemes and effective base point freeness (Popa)
status_evidence.snippet: The main problem is to give effective bounds for the base point freeness of linear series |L^p|; previous work by Le Potier and Hein gives bounds in the range of Fujita's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Effective bounds on k for |L^k| base-point free are known but not sharp at k=2 for general r.
